description: WANDa health check 1.0: stand-alone intake gate and static report on a delivery as received (after the converter, before any app import). The newest models set vs the newest WANDa GIS set (wanda_network_v1): static GIS and model data only - no PLDR results, model runs or flows. Facts only, no flags: the engineer reviews and decides each model's outcome; the tool proposes only engineer_review (model unreadable / names not checked). Written only by wanda_import health.

container.set_name: derived\health\<YYYY-MM-DD>_health (the dated snapshot; one set a day; a same-day rerun supersedes)

reports.estate: Intake_Health_<YYYY-MM-DD>.xlsx (Summary, Models, DMAs, Valve_differences, Data_quality, Notes)
reports.model: Health_<model_name>_<YYYY-MM-DD>.xlsx per model (DMAs, Pipes, Valves, Hydrants, Meters, Regulators, Pumps, Tanks)
reports.sheets: openpyxl write_only; one header row, frozen panes, autofilter; a list over row_limit rows continues in a <sheet>_2 sheet (the CSVs have no row limit)

fields.carried_from: the health set carried models' rows were copied from (new_model; null = none)
fields.files: the CSV files of the set (kind -> file)
fields.gis: GIS totals: real DMAs, in-network DMA pipes, isolation valves, valve placement counts
fields.models: [{model_name, file, size, mtime, name_ok (wanda_names rule), status, checked_at, carried}]
models set name (wanda_client check reports STALE on a newer one of either)

rules._note: values used (defaults in wanda_import health.py RULES, recorded in every set's wanda_health.json); rule_text says them in words
rules.names_checked_min_pct: model pipe names linking to GIS FIDs below this % -> names_checked no (50)
rules.modelled_min_length_pct: coverage modelled at or above this % of the in-network DMA length (50)
rules.model_shut: the model valve's ACTUAL state: OperationMode 0 = shut; otherwise InitialPosition (tau) <= tau_shut_max = shut, else open (throttled = open); no control row / NULL tau (OperationMode not 0) = not compared
rules.gis_shut: normal_position code list attribute shut = true; open = code open; throttled / unknown / blank = not compared
rules.boundary: DMAs of a valve = its dma_ref + the dma_refs of the in-network pipes at its node_ref; when node_ref is blank, its dma_ref + every DMA polygon within polygon_distance_m
rules.outcome: engineer_review when a model is unreadable or its names were not checked; otherwise blank

rule_text: GIS: in network = status attribute in_network (blank = in network); isolation valve = valve_type attribute isolates (blank = isolates); shut = normal_position attribute shut; real DMA = dma_areas area_type attribute is_dma.
A model element links to a GIS id by the shared rule (wanda_common/wanda_ids): name exact, else <FID>_<n> piece (pipes only), else description; defects are id_defects rows (engineer review).
A DMA row exists from one in-network GIS pipe of the DMA linked by the model; coverage modelled or edge; a real DMA no model touches gets one row with model_name '-'.

Valve DMAs: the valve's dma_ref + the dma_refs of the in-network pipes at its node_ref; the 1 m polygon placement only when node_ref is blank. A valve touching more than one DMA is a boundary valve, counted and listed against every DMA it touches.
names_checked no: the model row only (counts); no DMA rows or lists; proposed engineer_review.

new_gis: every model of the newest models set checked; new_model: the named models checked, every other model's rows (and its workbook) carried from the last health set of this layout (each keeps checked_at).
dma_items lists FIDs for modelled DMAs only (valves differing, pipes missing, id defects).

Facts only: no flags or thresholds on differences; the engineer decides. Only FIDs, DMA refs, codes, counts and model names are written; properties are counted, never listed; the GIS and the models are never changed.

types.code: a code from the field's code list

reader_rules: read by header name, ignore unknown columns (later columns are appended)
blank = not checked / not known, never 0
review only: never refuse, score or plan on it
